title: Four Killed in Manipur as Firewood Collectors Ambushed, Protesters Reach CM's Gate
excerpt: Three villagers were shot dead near the Imphal East-Kangpokpi border and a fourth man died after firing at a musical event, sparking protests that placed bodies outside Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh's bungalow.
body:
• At least four people were killed in two separate incidents in Manipur since Sunday night, including three villagers ambushed while collecting firewood near the Imphal East-Kangpokpi border.
  • The dead were identified as Arubam Ronil, 35, Lairenlakpam Inaobi, 51, and Kshetrimayum Sushil, 32; three others were injured and three people were reported missing, officials told PTI.
  • Angry locals placed bodies outside Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh's bungalow in Imphal; police used tear gas and a lathi-charge before the bodies were moved to JNIMS.
  • The chief minister visited the injured in hospital but did not respond to media queries; a local MLA demanded removal of a nearby Suspension of Operations camp, and police have not publicly confirmed who carried out the ambush.

At least four people have been killed in fresh violence in Manipur, in two separate incidents since Sunday night that brought Imphal to a near standstill on Monday. In the deadliest attack, three villagers who had gone to collect firewood in the hills were shot dead in an ambush near Khamenlok in Imphal East district, according to NDTV. In a separate incident, violence erupted during a musical event in a locality inhabited by Meiteis and Pangal Muslims, where stone-pelting and gunfire left several people injured and a 24-year-old man later died of bullet injuries.

The Firewood Ambush

A group of 16 people went to the hills near their village at around 7 a.m. to collect firewood when they were allegedly ambushed by armed militants in the Khongbal Sunurok Uyok area along the border of Kangpokpi and Imphal East districts, PTI quoted officials as saying, in reporting carried by Jagran. The deceased were identified as Arubam Ronil (35), Lairenlakpam Inaobi (51) and Kshetrimayum Sushil (32). Ronil and Inaobi died on the spot, while Sushil succumbed to his injuries at a private hospital. Three other people were injured and three were reported missing, according to officials. The injured undergoing treatment include N Suraj (19), Meisnam Somendro (53) and K Bosan (45).

Police sources told NDTV the area has a presence of Kuki militant groups. That is an allegation about presence, not a confirmed attribution: no group had claimed the attack in the reporting available on Monday, and officials had not publicly named those responsible.

Protest at the Chief Minister's Gate

Following the killings, angry locals marched to the state capital and placed the bodies outside the main gate of Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh's residence in Babupara, Imphal. The sudden arrival caught security personnel by surprise. Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells and resorted to a lathi-charge to disperse the crowd, after which the bodies were taken to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS). Protests spread elsewhere in the capital: a road was blocked at Khurai Lamlong, women demonstrated at the Ema Keithel market, and markets and shops across Imphal shut.

The Official Response — and the Other Side of the Argument

Chief Minister Singh visited the injured undergoing treatment at Raj Medicity Hospital, according to NDTV, and also visited the injured after the protest, but did not respond to media queries, Jagran reported. Security was tightened around the chief minister's bungalow and on roads leading to it, and security agencies sanitised the site of the fatal shooting.

Local MLA Thokchom Lokeshor Singh demanded immediate intervention by the authorities and the removal of a Suspension of Operations (SoO) camp — identified as Sinai Camp — situated near the area. He said the victims had gone to collect firewood near the boundary between Imphal East and Kuki-dominated Kangpokpi district, and that Assam Rifles personnel had assured the firewood collectors they would be protected. Those claims, and the demand to remove the camp, are the MLA's account; the Assam Rifles and the state government had not issued a detailed public response to them in the reporting available on Monday, and no Kuki organisation had commented on the allegation that Kuki militants carried out the ambush.

A Fragile Calm, Broken Again

Manipur's ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki communities erupted in May 2023 and has left relations strained ever since, with buffer areas along district boundaries remaining sensitive. NDTV noted that, given the location near the Imphal East-Kangpokpi boundary, further escalation could undermine the fragile calm. What happens next depends on whether the three missing villagers are found, whether police identify and arrest the attackers, and whether the state government answers the MLA's demand on the SoO camp. For residents of Nongshum and surrounding villages, the immediate question is more basic: whether a routine trip to collect firewood can be made without an armed escort.
